reviews.body: Verified against the head SHA and slack-sdk 3.41.0: `default_retry_handlers()` is connection-error only and `ConnectionErrorRetryHandler` explicitly refuses `HTTPError` responses, so a 429 really does reach `_outbound_retry_delay` as `SlackApiError` with `status_code`/`headers`, and the duck-typed parser matches the real `SlackResponse` shape. The wait rides the shared loop's `await asyncio.sleep` (non-blocking, no `time.sleep`), the `max(base, min(hint, 60))` precedence mirrors the Telegram flood-hint policy, and the send-file/connection-reply gaps are acknowledged in the docs. The new test file is red at base (imports `SLACK_MAX_OUTBOUND_RETRY_DELAY_SECONDS`, which does not exist there) and all 10 tests pass offline against this head with the retry sleep patched; ruff check/format are clean. Two minor findings only.

Re-review of 383a2ecd (delta since 1395f089: one docs commit). Both earlier nits are resolved: `backend/app/channels/AGENTS.md` and `docs/guide/im-channels.md` now name the Working-on-it acknowledgment (`_send_running_reply`) among the try-once call sites. The implementation (`slack.py` + `test_slack_send_retry_after.py`) is unchanged from the verified-good revision, so the earlier verification (slack-sdk default handlers are connection-error only; the shared `_outbound_retry_delay` override and the 60s cap behave as described, with non-blocking `asyncio.sleep` in the shared retry loop) still holds. One new finding on the changelog hunk this commit adds.

review_comments.body: Minor convention nit: this is a user-facing behavior change, but the change set does not touch CHANGELOG.md. Recent fix PRs (e.g. #8047, #8053, #8019) each add their own entry under `## [Unreleased]`. Could you add a short entry (Fixed group) describing the Slack 429 wait?

Doc-precision nit: the "try once" enumeration misses `_send_running_reply` in `backend/app/channels/slack.py` — the "Working on it..." acknowledgment is another `chat_postMessage` call site that gets a 429 and still tries once, but neither this bullet nor the `docs/guide/im-channels.md` one names it. Suggest something like "File uploads, connection replies, and the Working-on-it acknowledgment still try once."

Please drop this hunk: since #8202 landed, [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/bytedance/deer-flow/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) asks contributors not to touch `CHANGELOG.md`/`CHANGELOG_zh.md` — maintainers add the entry at merge time, and it explicitly says "If your PR touches the changelog, a reviewer will ask you to drop that hunk". (My earlier request to add an entry predated that rule; the merge-time convention supersedes it, and the Unreleased section moves fast enough that this hunk is likely to conflict.) It also updates only the English file, which is exactly the en/zh drift the rule exists to prevent. Everything else in the PR is unaffected.

**[P2] Keep Slack rate-limit waits off the shared inbound workers**

The shared inbound worker awaits outbound Slack delivery before taking another provider’s message. In a deterministic worker-pool probe, five rate-limited Slack replies occupied every default worker for two 60-second waits, leaving other-provider traffic queued. Base used short delays in the same probe. Defer long waits to bounded provider-specific delivery or limit inline sleep to the worker budget.

comments.body:
Added the Unreleased / Fixed entry and named the Working-on-it acknowledgment (`_send_running_reply`) in both documentation notes. The 10 Slack retry tests pass.
This comment was drafted with Claude Code.

Dropped the CHANGELOG.md hunk added in 383a2ec. CONTRIBUTING asks contributors not to edit CHANGELOG.md or CHANGELOG_zh.md, because maintainers add the entry at merge time; this also avoids an English-only Unreleased line. CHANGELOG_zh.md was not modified. The documentation notes that name the Working-on-it acknowledgment are unchanged. The Slack retry tests still pass (10 passed).

This comment was drafted with an AI coding assistant.

Thanks, agreed. Taking the inline-budget route: the Slack wait is now capped at 15 s (`SLACK_MAX_OUTBOUND_RETRY_DELAY_SECONDS`), so a rate-limited reply can no longer hold a shared inbound worker for 60 s. If Slack's `Retry-After` exceeds that budget, the send is abandoned with a warning log and the 429 propagates (no sleep, no early retry that Slack would reject again). Hints within the budget behave as before. Tests cover over-budget (no sleep, no post), at-budget, and the existing paths; docs and AGENTS.md updated.

This comment was drafted with Claude Code.
